For a new public extension point these need at least a description and `@since 6.1`."}, {"file": "junit-jupiter-api/src/main/java/org/junit/jupiter/api/io/TempDirDeletionStrategy.java", "line": 81, "category": "bug", "severity": "medium", "comment": "`IgnoreFailures` only ignores failures that the delegate reports inside the returned `DeletionResult`. An `IOException` thrown by `delegate.delete(...)` propagates out of this method unchanged, so deletion failures surfaced as exceptions (the declared `@throws IOException in case of general failures`) are not ignored. If the intent is \"never fail the test because of cleanup\", the delegate call should be wrapped in a try/catch and logged like the unsuccessful-result case."}, {"file": "junit-jupiter-api/src/main/java/org/junit/jupiter/api/io/TempDirDeletionStrategy.java", "line": 121, "category": "question", "severity": "medium", "comment": "`tempDir.toRealPath()` (and `tryToResetPermissions` just below) will throw `NoSuchFileException` if the directory no longer exists, e.g. when a test already deleted its own temp dir. Is `delete` intended to require an existing directory? If so it would be worth stating in the interface Javadoc; otherwise an early return for a non-existent path seems safer for a public extension point."}, {"file": "junit-jupiter-api/src/main/java/org/junit/jupiter/api/io/TempDirDeletionStrategy.java", "line": 189, "category": "style", "severity": "low", "comment": "The anonymous `SimpleFileVisitor` already captures `fileOperations` from the enclosing method, so taking it as a parameter here (and shadowing the captured variable) adds noise at every call site. Dropping the parameter would make the visitor read more cleanly."}]

[{"file": "junit-jupiter-engine/src/main/java/org/junit/jupiter/engine/extension/TempDirectory.java", "line": 193, "category": "design", "severity": "medium", "comment": "Unlike `determineTempDirFactory` below, which instantiates the factory eagerly when the temp dir is created, the strategy class is only instantiated when the supplier is called at cleanup time. A misconfigured `deletionStrategy` (no accessible no-arg constructor, abstract class, throwing constructor) will therefore fail during close instead of failing fast at injection, where the error is much easier to attribute. Was the lazy instantiation deliberate?"}]
